subtasks.description:
Create tests in internal/agentmon/exitlog_test.go that define the expected behavior of the exit log subsystem BEFORE implementation. Tests should cover:

1. TestParseExitLogEntry — parse a valid JSONL line into an ExitLogEntry struct with fields: AgentID, TaskID, Timestamp, ExitReason, LastTool, LastTarget, FilesModified, CommitsMade, Summary.
2. TestWriteExitLogEntry — write an ExitLogEntry to a JSONL file and verify the output format.
3. TestReadExitLog — read multiple entries from a JSONL file, verify correct parsing and ordering.
4. TestReadExitLog_MissingFile — returns nil/empty slice and no error when file doesn't exist.
5. TestReadExitLog_MalformedLines — gracefully skips malformed lines while parsing valid ones.

The ExitLogEntry struct should contain: AgentID (string), TaskID (string), Timestamp (time.Time), ExitReason (string — one of 'success', 'error', 'context_limit', 'user_interrupt', 'unknown'), LastTool (string), LastTarget (string), FilesModified ([]string), CommitsMade (int), Summary (string).

The JSONL file should be written to <projectDir>/exit-log.jsonl.

All tests should initially FAIL since the implementation doesn't exist yet.

Use testutil helpers where applicable (t.TempDir for file paths). Do NOT define local test helpers that duplicate testutil functionality.

subtasks.description:
Create internal/agentmon/exitlog.go with the exit log data model and JSONL read/write functions. This file lives in the agentmon package so that the agent/ package (which already imports agentmon) can use it without adding a new internal/ import.

Implement:
1. ExitLogEntry struct with JSON tags: agent_id, task_id, timestamp, exit_reason, last_tool, last_target, files_modified, commits_made, summary.
2. ExitReason string constants: ExitSuccess, ExitError, ExitContextLimit, ExitUserInterrupt, ExitUnknown.
3. WriteExitLogEntry(projectDir string, entry ExitLogEntry) error — appends a single JSONL line to <projectDir>/exit-log.jsonl. Creates file if it doesn't exist. Uses json.Marshal + file append.
4. ReadExitLog(projectDir string) ([]ExitLogEntry, error) — reads all entries from exit-log.jsonl. Returns empty slice (not error) if file doesn't exist. Skips malformed lines with a logged warning.
5. ExitLogPath(projectDir string) string — returns the path to exit-log.jsonl.

Keep the file well under 200 lines. Use encoding/json from stdlib. No new internal/ imports needed (agentmon already imports ctxmon, but this file won't need it).

Make the pre-written tests in exitlog_test.go pass. Do NOT modify the tests.

subtasks.description:
Create tests in internal/agent/hook_test.go that define the expected behavior of the hook infrastructure BEFORE implementation. Tests should cover:

1. TestGenerateExitLogScript — verify that generateExitLogScript(agentID, taskID, projectDir) returns a valid bash script that:
   - Reads the latest .jsonl transcript from projectDir
   - Extracts last tool_use entry (tool name and target)
   - Reads agent-metadata.json for agent_id and task_id
   - Writes a JSONL line to <projectDir>/exit-log.jsonl
   - Is executable (starts with #!/bin/bash)

2. TestWriteAgentMetadata — verify that writeAgentMetadata(claudeDir, agentID, taskID) writes a JSON file at <claudeDir>/agent-metadata.json containing {"agent_id": "<uuid>", "task_id": "<uuid>"}.

3. TestSettingsJSONIncludesStopHook — verify that the settings.json generation includes a Stop hook entry pointing to the exit-log script path, in addition to the existing Notification and PreCompact hooks.

4. TestEnrichCompletionWithExitLog — verify that enrichCompletion reads exit log entries from the project dir and populates Completion.ExitInfo with the latest matching entry for the agent.

Use t.TempDir() for paths. All tests should initially FAIL.

IMPORTANT: The Completion struct enhancement adds an ExitInfo field (pointer to ExitLogEntry from agentmon package). This avoids adding a new internal/ import to the agent package since it already imports agentmon.

subtasks.description:
Modify internal/agent/runner.go and create internal/agent/hooks.go to add the Stop hook infrastructure.

In internal/agent/hooks.go (new file, ~120 lines):
1. generateExitLogScript(agentID, taskID, projectDir string) string — returns a bash script that:
   - Finds the latest .jsonl in projectDir
   - Uses tail + grep + basic JSON extraction to get last tool_use name and target
   - Reads agent-metadata.json for structured IDs
   - Counts modified files via git diff in the worktree
   - Appends a JSONL entry to <projectDir>/exit-log.jsonl
   - Handles missing files gracefully (|| true patterns)
2. writeAgentMetadata(claudeDir string, agentID, taskID uuid.UUID) error — writes agent-metadata.json.
3. stopHookEntry(scriptPath string) map[string]any — returns the Stop hook config for settings.json.
4. enrichCompletion(comp *Completion, projectDir string, agentID uuid.UUID) — reads exit log via agentmon.ReadExitLog, finds the latest entry matching agentID, sets comp.ExitInfo.

In internal/agent/runner.go (modify):
1. Enhance Completion struct: add ExitInfo *agentmon.ExitLogEntry field.
2. In the worktree setup section (near line 348-387), after building the hooks map:
   - Call writeAgentMetadata to write agent-metadata.json
   - Generate exit-log.sh script and write to claudeDir
   - Add Stop hook to the hooks map via stopHookEntry
3. In the completion path (where Completion is sent to channel), call enrichCompletion to populate ExitInfo from the exit log JSONL.

Constraints:
- runner.go is 630 lines; keep additions minimal (~20 lines of wiring)
- hooks.go should stay under 150 lines
- No new internal/ imports (agentmon is already imported)
- Use ctxmon.ProjectDirName to derive projectDir from worktreePath (ctxmon already imported)

Make the pre-written tests in hook_test.go pass. Do NOT modify the tests.

subtasks.description:
Final integration subtask that verifies all components work together end-to-end and updates documentation.

1. Verify the full data flow:
   - Agent spawns → settings.json includes Stop hook → agent-metadata.json written
   - Agent exits → Stop hook fires exit-log.sh → exit-log.jsonl written to project-dir
   - Orchestrator drains completion → enrichCompletion reads exit-log.jsonl → ExitInfo populated
   - processAgentResult stores exit info in Agent.Config
   - TUI detail view displays exit reason

2. Run full test suite: go test ./... — all tests must pass.

3. Run constitution checks: bash scripts/check_constitution.sh
   - Verify no file length violations
   - Verify no new internal/ import ceiling violations
   - Verify gofmt compliance

4. Update documentation:
   - Add a section to README.md (or relevant docs) describing the agent exit logging feature:
     - What it captures (exit reason, last tool, summary)
     - Where logs are stored (~/.claude/projects/<dir>/exit-log.jsonl)
     - How it surfaces in the TUI
   - Document the Stop hook configuration in the hooks documentation if any exists

5. Verify no regressions in existing hook behavior (idle_prompt, PreCompact still work).

This subtask connects the independently-built components and ensures the feature works as a whole. It should NOT introduce new business logic — only wiring, verification, and documentation.
